title: Naturality of iterated local Frobenius for morphisms of constructible Weil pairs
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb/\Ql$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$, with geometric Frobenius as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. All coefficient categories are the raw rationalized constructible categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and Weil pairs and their morphisms are those of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Use the specified natural pullback-composition and pullback/scalar comparisons, rationalized with their equality-of-morphisms and finite-iteration compatibilities, of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization].

Let $F/\Ql$ be finite inside $\Qlb$, let $n\geq1$, and let $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ with its specified geometric point $\bar x:s\to X$. Write $P=L\bar x_F^*$, $Q=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,F}$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $D=QP$, $G_r=L(g_X^r)_F^*$ and $S_r=L(g_s^r)_F^*$ for $r\geq1$. For a constructible point complex $N$, let $I_N^{[r]}:Q(N)\to Q(S_rN)$ be the $r$-fold point transport in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], using $\iota$ of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural]. Let
$$\rho_M:S_nP(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}PG_n(M),\qquad R(M)=Q(\rho_M)I_{P(M)}^{[n]}:D(M)\to D(G_nM),$$
where $\rho$ is the specified return comparison for $g_X^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$.

The following naturality assertions hold on the full constructible domain. For every morphism $w:N\to N'$ in $D^b_c(s,F)$ and $r\geq1$,
$$Q(S_rw)I_N^{[r]}=I_{N'}^{[r]}Q(w).$$
For every morphism $v:M\to M'$ in $D^b_c(X,F)$,
$$PG_n(v)\rho_M=\rho_{M'}S_nP(v),\qquad D(G_nv)R(M)=R(M')D(v).$$
For any two $F$-Weil pairs $(A,\alpha),(B,\beta)$ and any morphism of pairs $v:(A,\alpha)\to(B,\beta)$, so $v\alpha=\beta G_1(v)$, their specified iterated structure maps satisfy
$$v\alpha^{[r]}=\beta^{[r]}G_r(v)\quad(r\geq1).$$
Consequently their local operators $\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(A,\alpha)=D(\alpha^{[n]})R(A)$ and $\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(B,\beta)=D(\beta^{[n]})R(B)$ satisfy
$$D(v)\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(A,\alpha)=\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(B,\beta)D(v).$$
The morphism $v$ need not be invertible. No integral Weil-stable lattice or finite-reduction Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The prescribed localPullbackComposition of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] is natural. Its components are heterogeneous-equal to the localization of the components of the natural integral composition isomorphism [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition]. The object and pure-tensor map prescriptions of rationalDerivedPullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] show this equality of naturality squares on pure tensors. The integral naturality square and the tensor composition formula prove that case; additivity and tensor induction prove the general square. The inverse comparison is natural by cancelling its isomorphisms. Induct on the positive-power index in localPointTransportIterate: apply this inverse-comparison square, then the induction hypothesis to the one-step pullback of the arrow, then the single-step point-transport square. This proves the first clause with the actual specified recursion.

proof.text: The two composition comparisons in localConstructibleReturnComparison are natural by the tensor-induction calculation in step 2. The middle equality-of-scheme-morphisms comparison is natural by a general equality-of-functors naturality lemma, proved by equality elimination. Compose these three squares; this proves the second clause for the stipulated semilinear return equality, without asserting a fixed geometric point.

proof.text:
Apply $Q$ to step 3 and use step 2 with $w=P(v)$ and $r=n$. Functoriality, the definition $R(M)=Q(\rho_M)I_{P(M)}^{[n]}$, and these two equations give
$$\begin{aligned}
D(G_nv)R(M)&=Q(PG_n(v))Q(\rho_M)I_{P(M)}^{[n]}\\
&=Q(\rho_{M'})Q(S_nP(v))I_{P(M)}^{[n]}\\
&=Q(\rho_{M'})I_{P(M')}^{[n]}Q(P(v))=R(M')D(v).
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the asserted naturality of $R$ for every underlying morphism $v$.

proof.text: The defining algebra morphism condition of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] is the base case for localWeilIterate. For the successor, expand its actual recursion from [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], apply the induction hypothesis, combine the two maps under the power pullback functor, apply the one-step algebra morphism condition under that functor, and then apply the composition-comparison naturality square proved in step 2. Reassociate to obtain the fourth clause.

source.place: Displayed alternating-trace formula; agent-supplied induction on its iterated Weil-structure factor.

proof.text:
Finally apply the functor $D$ to the equality of step 5 at $r=n$, and multiply by $R(A)$. Step 4 applied to the underlying map of the Weil-pair morphism gives
$$\begin{aligned}
D(v)\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(A,\alpha)
&=D(v)D(\alpha^{[n]})R(A)\\
&=D(\beta^{[n]})D(G_nv)R(A)\\
&=D(\beta^{[n]})R(B)D(v)
=\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(B,\beta)D(v).
\end{aligned}$$
These are the local operators of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. No inverse of $v$ was used in any step. Every equality was obtained in the full rational constructible categories from the cited naturality and coherent-composition statements, so no Weil-stable integral lattice or condition on the Tor amplitude of finite reductions is needed.
